output.summary: An herbaceous perennial native to Japan, China and Korea, Japanese knotweed forms dense thickets from an extensive underground stem network. Its hollow, jointed stems resemble bamboo, and it bears small cream or white flowers in late summer and early autumn. Young stems are eaten raw or cooked as a spring vegetable, including as a wild food in Japan, and taste like lemony rhubarb.
output.edibilityNote: Young stems are eaten raw or cooked as a spring vegetable; they are foraged in Japan and used in European restaurant cuisine.
